claims.text: Multiphase refractory high-entropy alloys with BCC/B2 microstructures may undergo a ductile-brittle-ductile transition during isothermal aging.
The proposed transition occurs during aging at 600–800 °C for 10–100 hours.
The non-monotonic ductility transition is driven by B2 chemical ordering and redistribution of the BCC and B2 phase fractions.
A relevant initial microstructure can consist of fine ordered B2 regions or precipitates in a disordered BCC matrix.
A relevant initial microstructure can have cuboidal BCC pockets in a continuous ordered B2 matrix.
Water quenching after aging preserves the high-temperature phase fractions and aged microstructure.
Aging progressively increases the long-range order parameter of the B2 phase.
Long-term aging increases the B2 phase fraction at the expense of the BCC phase fraction.
The phase-fraction change moves the ductile BCC phase through a percolation threshold.
Greater B2 ordering or a continuous ordered B2 matrix increases alloy strength.
B2 ordering reduces ductility by restricting dislocation mobility in the ordered phase.
Extended aging produces coarser B2 precipitates.
Formation or restoration of a continuous disordered BCC matrix can provide good ductility despite a relatively high B2 fraction.
Longer aging may restore ductility by activating additional slip systems in the ordered B2 phase.
Elongation will decrease after approximately 20–50 hours and recover after more than 80 hours of aging.
The as-processed baseline has greater than 20% elongation because of its fine, disordered or partially ordered dual-phase microstructure.
The transition is restricted to BCC/B2 dual-phase alloys with VEC between 4.5 and 5.0.
Single-phase BCC and FCC alloys are not expected to exhibit the proposed non-monotonic aging transition.
RHEAs with VEC below 4.5 are intrinsically ductile, whereas alloys with VEC above 5.5 are intrinsically brittle.
AlCoCrFeNi2.1 is an example of a BCC/B2 dual-phase RHEA suitable for the proposed falsification experiment.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and boundary require a refractory BCC/B2 alloy, but the proposed AlCoCrFeNi2.1 test alloy is characterized by the cited evidence as a eutectic FCC/B2 HEA rather than a BCC/B2 RHEA.
